newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis AG new share issue seen 1-for-10.
newsitem.headline: Fortis AG new share issue seen 1-for-10.

text.p: Fortis AG, the Belgian arm of Belgian-Dutch insurance group Fortis, which announced a capital increase of 17 billion Belgian francs, would probably issue one new share for every ten existing shares, analysts said on Thursday.
"I think it will be one for ten shares or one for nine, but it is not official yet," said trader Pieter Vander Stichele at G-Securities.
Trader Benoit Kint at brokerage Petercam said he also expected Fortis to issue one new share for every 10 existing shares.
Fortis AG said on Wednesday the number of shares allowing for subscription to new shares and their price will be announced by February 11. Subscription will run from February 12 to 26.
Traders and analysts said Wednesday evening's announcement came as no surprise to the market.
"We all knew it would come up, but the amount is a bit more than we expected, we expected between 12 to 13 billion," said G-Securities' Vander Stichele.
Fortis AG's shares slipped on the news but traders did not expect any long-term impact. By 1245 GMT the share was down 0.71 percent at 5,560 francs in an overall lower Brussels market
"I don't see any major movement (in the price)," Petercam's Kint said.

Dealers said the capital increase would serve to pay for the Fortis group's recent acquisition of MeesPierson and its plan to increase its stake in Belgian state-owned bank and insurance group ASLK-CGER. Fortis AG owns 50 percent of Fortis. The remainder is held by Dutch Fortis AMEV.
"Usually when a capital increase is announced the market retreats a bit, but it all depends on the optimism on growth of the group, which in this case is positive," another trader said.
